text:
sam: Heads-up — noticed a lot of autoscaler churn this morning in eu-west. Two GPU nodepools (gpu-a100-spot, gpu-a100-ondemand) keep flipping during embedding batch bursts. Scale-up is fine, but scale-down kills hot nodes too quickly and we lose cache/KV; costs spike due to repeated warmups. Anyone else seeing this?

leo: saw the same in monitoring. spikes align with nightly batch jobs. dashboards show many short lived pods (2–8m). Current scale-down-unneeded-time looks low.

anya: what are the CA flags set to right now? expander? eviction thresholds?

sam: current autoscaler flags from deploy:```
--expander=least-waste 
--scale-down-unneeded-time=2m 
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 
--scan-interval=10s 
--max-empty-bulk-delete=10 
```
(we run the helm chart with these values in k8s/gpu/autoscaler-values.yaml)

morgan: two quick observations: 1) 2m unneeded is too aggressive for GPU workloads where jobs are bursty and startup is expensive (KV warm, model load). 2) least-waste often picks smallest leftover bin which can cause cross-pool oscillation between spot and ondemand pools.

anya: agree. In the past we used --expander=most-pods for better packing of GPU pods to reduce fragmentation. Also higher unneeded-time and scan-interval helps avoid flip-flop.

leo: what about a 'burst pool' pattern: keep a small buffer of on-demand GPUs with long TTL, let spot scale aggressively for long tasks, fallback to on-demand when spot quota unavailable. That reduces churn and keeps hot nodes alive for cache reuse.

sam: that makes sense. Proposed quick changes for a canary cluster:```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m 
--scan-interval=30s 
--expander=most-pods 
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.6 
--balance-similar-node-groups=true 
```
Thoughts?

morgan: +1 on 10m. bumping utilization threshold to 0.6 reduces evictions of semi-utilized GPU nodes. balance-similar-node-groups helps avoid moving pods between spot/ondemand pools.

anya: also check for DaemonSets and PDBs blocking scale-down. We had a case where node had kube-proxy metrics causing it to be considered non-empty. run:```
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep <node-name>
```
and ```
kubectl describe pod <pod>
```
for blockers.

autoscaler-bot: deploy started for autoscaler-canary (eu-west) with image v1.21.3-canary. log: "rolling update autoscaler 3/3 updated". :rocket:

leo: cost note — if we increase unneeded-time to 10m we keep nodes longer which raises baseline cost but should reduce repeated model loads and overall token cost per inference. I estimate ~8–12% net savings for high-burst workloads due to reduced warmup overhead.

sam: good to track. I'll create a Grafana panel for 'node churn rate' and 'average node alive time' + cost estimate per churn.

morgan: small ops checklist before canary: 1) patch helm values 2) run dry-run with kubeval 3) deploy to eu-west-canary 4) monitor churn, pod startup latency, and cost for 48h 5) rollback if scale-down rate > baseline

anya: one more idea — adjust PreferNoSchedule taint on burst scheduling to favor on-demand for long-running jobs. alternatively use pod affinity to pin large batching jobs to the burst pool.

sam: actionable items: - morgan will push helm change to infra repo (PR) - leo will add Grafana panels - anya will audit DaemonSets/PDBs on eu-west canary - i'll run the canary deploy and monitor 48h

morgan: pushing PR in 10m, will include the flag diffs and a short note on rollback commands. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/compare/patch-autoscaler-canary

leo: will add the panels and alert thresholds (churn rate > 15 nodes/hour).

sam: thanks team. if canary looks good we can roll to prod next week, otherwise we iterate. :thumbsup:

anya: FYI — spotted a pod that was preventing scale-down earlier: metrics-exporter (runAsNonRoot) created ephemeral volume that lingered. I'll clean up and add to docs.

autoscaler-bot: canary finished rollout on eu-west-canary at 1955554388 — monitoring hooks active.

sam: closing loop tomorrow AM with results. if you see odd behaviour ping here or @oncall.
